title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi/parallel calls, injection, and retries
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: customers are authoring tool schemas that request multiple tools in a single turn and expect the runtime to run tools in parallel when safe, inject tool outputs back into the model prompt in a consistent, structured way, and apply predictable retry semantics for transient tool failures. Current behavior required ad-hoc workarounds in user code and led to duplicated requests and confusing OpenAI-compat responses. This PR improves execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool calls, standardizes tool result injection (both streaming and non-streaming), and implements a bounded retry policy for transient tool errors. It also includes small adjustments to the OpenAI compatibility layer to preserve function-call structured outputs across retries and backoff. Changes: - Add executor-level parallelism for independent tool calls with deterministic ordering for injection. - Implement a ToolResultEnvelope that normalizes tool outputs into structured tokens for streaming and non-streaming paths. - Add bounded exponential backoff retry policy (configurable per-tool) with idempotency key support so retries are safe. - Update openai_compat layer to serialize function_call results consistently across retries and when partial results are streamed. - Improve streaming stability by flushing tool-injection checkpoints to the stream to avoid truncated or out-of-order structured objects when a retry occurs mid-stream. - Add end-to-end integration tests covering parallel tool execution, injection ordering, and retry behavior under transient failures. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `tool_exec_ergonomics_v1`. Rollout a small percentage of traffic for 48 hours; watch structured-output regression alerts and streaming error rates. If increased errors observed, rollback to previous flag. Related: builds on design work in ENG-4211 and follows up on incident postmortem SUP-332. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-4211) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs update - [x] SDK compatibility adjustments Notes: the implementation intentionally maintains deterministic injection ordering by capturing the original tool request order and using it as the canonical sequence for injection even when calls are executed in parallel. This avoids surprising permutations in structured outputs for consumers that depend on index-based fields.
commits: feat(executor): parallelize independent tool calls with ordering guarantees
feat(streaming): ToolResultEnvelope and checkpointed injection for streaming paths
feat(retries): bounded exponential backoff + idempotency key plumbing
chore(openai-compat): preserve function_call payloads across retries and streams
test: add integration tests for parallel tool calls and retry scenarios
files_changed: docs/openapi/tool-calling.md  (document ordered injection and retry semantics)
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can we make the retry backoff parameters per-tool-configurable? Some external services have rate limits. — Aisha: yes, added tooling config and defaults; documentation updated to cover config examples.

Sara Kim: Concerned about ordering when we parallelize. If we keep canonical ordering we should document it clearly to avoid client assumptions breaking. — Aisha: updated docs/openapi/tool-calling.md and added unit tests asserting canonical ordering preserved after parallel execution.

Liam O'Connor: Integration test flaky on CI (flaky_stream). Looks like a race when stream writer checkpoint is flushed. — Aisha: fixed race by serializing checkpoint writes using stream writer mutex; reran CI and test passed.
Diego Martinez: Suggest adding a metrics tag for retry_count per-tool so we can alert on elevated retries. — Aisha: added retry_count metric and dashboard tile.
Sara Kim: small nits on Python SDK compatibility function names. — Aisha: renamed helpers and added compatibility shim for one release cycle.
release_notes:
- Improved tool-calling ergonomics: parallel execution of independent tools with deterministic injection ordering.
- Structured tool result envelope for stable streaming & non-streaming outputs.
- Configurable bounded retries with idempotency keys for transient tool failures.
- OpenAI-compat layer updated to preserve function_call payloads across retries/streams.
test_plan: Unit tests for executor and retry policy; integration tests simulate transient tool failures and verify deterministic injection ordering; end-to-end smoke using python and typescript SDKs. CI run passed after addressing flaky_stream race. Deployed behind feature flag and will be rolled out gradually.
additional_context: This PR complements previous PRs around tool-calling ergonomics (see pr-30122 and pr-29345). The feature is behind a flag to allow canary rollout and zero-downtime rollback. Observability added to monitor retry spikes and structured-output regressions.
